passage: Critic: The new museum wing is a failure. Attendance in its first month was lower than attendance at the old wing's opening twenty years ago.
question: The critic's reasoning is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that it:
options: ignores that circumstances may have changed considerably over twenty years
attacks the architect rather than the building
presupposes what it sets out to prove
uses the word 'failure' in two different senses

passage: If the council approves the budget, the park will be renovated. The park will not be renovated.
question: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?
options: The council approved the budget.
The council did not approve the budget.
The park will be renovated next year.
The budget was too small.

passage: Every employee who completed the safety course received a certificate. Maria received a certificate, so Maria must have completed the safety course.
question: The reasoning in the argument is flawed because the argument:
options: assumes that only those who completed the course could have received a certificate
relies on the testimony of an interested party
generalizes from a single unrepresentative case
confuses a cause with its effect

passage: Towns that built new bike lanes saw a drop in traffic accidents. Therefore, building bike lanes reduces accidents.
question: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: Some towns without bike lanes also saw fewer accidents.
The towns that built bike lanes lowered their speed limits at the same time.
Bike lanes are expensive to build.
Cyclists prefer roads with bike lanes.

passage: No reptile is warm-blooded. All snakes are reptiles.
question: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?
options: Some warm-blooded animals are snakes.
No snake is warm-blooded.
All reptiles are snakes.
Some reptiles are warm-blooded.
